project.description: Fit-out of a 400 m² office: design, permit, new partitions, services, finishes, furniture and IT.
project.name: Tutorial: office fit-out

notes.actions: PM to call the supplier on Monday. Client to give socket positions by Wednesday.
notes.issues: Furniture supplier has not confirmed the delivery date.
notes.look_ahead: Partitions, electrical first fix and the start of ceilings.
notes.progress: Permit granted. Strip out complete. Partition walls half done (set out, studs and tracks).
notes.summary: Design and approvals are done; strip out finished and the partitions have started.

risks.name: Furniture delivered late
risks.response: Weekly call with the supplier; keep a local back-up quote

sections.text: Furniture delivery is the main risk; see the risk register.
sections.title: Notes

tour.builder: The Report Builder makes your own report from sections. "Weekly client report" is saved with this plan: key figures, the S-curve, work completed, the next two weeks, milestones and a note.
tour.calendar: The Calendar view shows the tasks on a month grid. Working time comes from Project › Change Working Time: this plan's Standard calendar has a public holiday in week 6, and a Six-day week calendar is given to Painting (Task Calendar).
tour.checks: Checks test the plan's quality (open ends, constraints, long tasks, negative float, missing baseline…), like a scheduling audit. Click a line to go to the tasks.
tour.dashboard:
Project is the built-in dashboard: key figures, the S-curve across the page and the cards that have data (Cards ▾ to choose).

Client dashboard is your own: tiles with formulas (SPI turns red below 1), a progress ring, the budget from the Weekly report sheet and the team's countries. Edit layout to move or resize tiles.
tour.gantt:
The Gantt chart is where the plan is built. Each row is a task: indent a row (Alt+Shift+→) to put it under a summary such as Design or Construction.

• Links: Predecessors "16SS+2d" starts Electrical first fix 2 days after the walls start; "18FS+1d" leaves a day for ceilings to set before painting.
• Milestones (0 days) mark approvals and handover; three are on the timeline above.
• Furniture order has a Start No Earlier Than; Handover has a deadline (green arrow).
• Permit review is 7 elapsed days (it runs over the weekend).
• Feature wall is inactive: kept, but not scheduled.
• Weekly site meeting is a recurring task (Task › Recurring).
• Days left and Health are your own columns with formulas; Health turns red with conditional formatting (Format › Conditional Formatting).
tour.lookahead: The Look-ahead lists the next weeks' work and the constraint log: what each task still needs before it can start (socket positions from the client, paint colours). Add items with + and close them when they arrive.
tour.manpower: Manpower counts people on site per day by trade (the resource groups): what you would show in a site meeting or a tender.
tour.network: The Network Diagram draws the same logic as boxes and arrows. Red boxes are critical: delay one and the handover moves. Try Format › Box style, or bands by WBS.
tour.portfolio:
Portfolio lists every plan in a folder with its finish, progress and health, so you can see all your projects at once. Save this tutorial in a folder with other plans and choose that folder here.

That is the tour. Hide these notes with × (Help › Tutorial notes brings them back).
tour.progress: The weekly progress report: figures for the week against the last one, what was done and what is next, and the notes written for week 5 (summary, issues, actions). Print it or save it as HTML for the client.
tour.reports: Ready-made reports: tasks, costs, resources, milestones, critical path and more. Each prints or saves as HTML.
tour.ressheet:
The Resources sheet lists the team with rates, groups and countries (the flags on the dashboard). Paint is a material (12 per litre, 40 litres on Painting); Permit fee is a cost resource (1,500 on the permit review).

Double-click Electrician › Working Time: two days of annual leave. Resource calendars are on (Project › Schedule Options), so Electrical first fix works round the leave; the permit review ignores resource calendars.
tour.resusage: Resource Usage shows each person's hours by day. Red means more than they can give: use Resource › Level to move work, or look at Res. Usage by trade.
tour.risks: The risk register: furniture delivered late (7 days, likely) and asbestos found during strip out (5 days, less likely). Each is linked to its task, so the schedule risk analysis can use it.
tour.scurve: S-curves: planned (the baseline) against actual, built from the five closed weeks, and the forecast to the finish. Switch the weight between duration, cost, hours and physical %.
tour.setup:
This plan is a small office fit-out, filled in from start to finish so you can see every part of Datum Plan at work. Open each view in the sidebar, top to bottom; this note changes with the view.

Setup holds the project's facts: name, code FIT-01, client, manager, location, and the activity ID prefix (A). The start date is a Monday five weeks ago and the status date is last Friday, so the plan is in the middle of the work.
tour.sheets:
Sheets work like Excel inside the plan. The Weekly report reads the plan by name (=ProjectFinish, =PercentComplete, =SPI), counts late tasks with =COUNTIF(Tasks[Late],TRUE), lists the milestones with FILTER, and keeps a small budget by item.

Click a cell to see its formula; type = and click Plan Data to pick a field. Nothing is copied by hand: the numbers follow the plan.
tour.simrisk: Schedule Risk runs the plan a thousand times with each task's range (Optimistic and Pessimistic duration, set on five tasks here) and the risks' chances. It shows how likely each handover date is (P50, P80) and which tasks drive it. Click Run.
tour.taskusage: Task Usage spreads each task's hours over the days: who works on it and how much. The Builder works 300 % (three people) on Strip out.
tour.team: The Team Planner shows each person's tasks on one line. Drag a task to another person or day to reassign it.
tour.tracking:
The Tracking Gantt compares today's plan with the baseline (grey bars), saved before any work started (Project › Set Baseline).

Furniture manufacture is at 35 % when the baseline expected more, and the partitions are half done, so their bars run late against the grey ones and the finish moves. % labels show how far each task has got.
tour.update:
Update is where progress goes in each week. This plan was updated five times: Update Project marked the work done to each Friday, then the real differences were typed in (furniture manufacture at 35 %, the partitions behind).

Partition walls use a rule of credit: four weighted steps (Set out 10 %, Studs 40 %, Boards 35 %, Finish 15 %), so ticking a step gives the physical % complete. Close period stores each week for the S-curves.
